title: Commit Suggestion Engine for Dedicated Pools
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: customers with Dedicated pools struggle to choose commit sizes that balance cost and throughput. Current manual heuristics lead to overprovisioning (wasted spend) or undercommit (throughput throttles and SLO misses) during bursts. Goal: ship a suggestion engine that analyzes historical utilization, SLO targets, model footprints and workload shape to recommend a safe, confidence-scored commit value and a short actionable plan (resize, autoscale policy tweak, or workload routing change).

Scope and deliverables:
- Data ingestion: daily utilization histograms (per-tenant, per-pool), request size distribution, 50/95/99 latency & tail token rates, model memory/latency profiles, and scheduled maintenance windows.
- Right-sizing algorithm: produce a suggested commit with a confidence band and recommended headroom. Core idea: 95th-percentile demand simulation + tenant-aware slab packing to avoid noisy-neighbor regressions. Include adjustable safety factor based on customer tier (enterprise vs. dev).
- Simulation runner: run a Monte Carlo (or deterministic percentile) simulation to estimate SLO risk at different commit levels and output expected cost delta.
- UI & API: a console panel that shows a suggested commit, expected monthly savings, estimated SLO impact, and one-click apply workflow (creates change request to ops or auto-applies for approved tenants). Also provide an API endpoint for programmatic suggestions.
- Alerts & recommendations: emit actionable alerts when observed utilization diverges from committed profile (e.g., sustained 15% overcommit exposures for 6 hours).

Non-goals: not replacing full autoscaler or making final billing changes. This is advisory and integrates with existing autoscale controls and rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: Suggestion engine ingests 14 days of historical per-tenant utilization and request histograms and stores aggregated summaries.
Algorithm outputs a suggested commit with confidence band and expected cost delta for at least three sample tenants in staging.
Console shows suggestion, a one-click action to open a change request with pre-filled rationale, and a link to simulation details.
API endpoint /v1/dedicated/suggestions returns JSON (curl-friendly) containing suggestion, confidence, and estimated SLO risk (staging-only).
Simulation runner produces an SLO-risk vs commit curve and the job completes within 30s for a tenant with 30-day history in staging infra.
Integration tests that validate suggestion is conservative when synthetic spike patterns are injected (no false 'shrink' suggestions under bursty workloads).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Raman: Kickoff notes. Product asked for an advisory feature (non-destructive) that lowers spend by nudging customers to smaller commits when safe. PM: Maya Lopez. Key constraint: suggestions must not trigger SLA violations.
2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Initial data map completed. Found gaps in per-tenant tail-latency aggregation for older tenants; will add a short ETL to calculate 95/99 token-rate histograms.

2026-03-05 - Maya Lopez (PM): Prioritized that enterprise tenants get an 'apply with approval' flow while self-serve tenants can opt into auto-apply after a 30-day trial. Added label 'needs-legal-review' if auto-apply enabled for multi-tenant pools.

2026-03-08 - Eng lead review: Decided to implement two simulation modes: deterministic percentile-based fast path (primary) and Monte Carlo night-job (secondary) for higher confidence. Trade-off: Monte Carlo more accurate but expensive. We'll expose both in staging.

2026-03-10 - Design sync: Suggested console wireframe and an explainer tooltip for safety factor; design will hand off assets by 2026-03-16. UX asks for an 'why this number' expandable explanation showing key signals.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Built prototype that computes 95th-percentile slot demand and returns a suggested commit. Current prototype uses 14-day rolling window. Next: add tenant-aware packing and confidence scoring and run against 5 internal tenants in staging.
2026-03-12 - Security note (Nate H.): Reviewed data access model. No new secrets required, but ensure suggestions do not leak tenant ids in aggregated telemetry exposed to other customers.
